title: Reuse cached page sections
goal: Reuse static SSR output safely across requests.

selectionNotes: Static SSR only; cache hits skip child lifecycle; isolate user-specific markup.

prerequisites: Use the .NET 11 Web SDK/runtime with C# 15.0 and the locked sample assets. No workload, external service or experimental opt-in.
Authenticate before rendering. Keep fresh authorization and per-request content outside CacheView; vary every value that changes cached output.
Framework Components/Endpoints assemblies; SDK-aligned Internal.Assets 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105; optional HybridCache 10.11.0 net10.0 asset is executed by this net11.0 server.
Default CacheView memory store, or HybridCache local memory without IDistributedCache; both executed.
ASP.NET Core server; Windows x64 execution. Other OS and multi-node providers untested.
Static SSR GET only. Interactive rendering and CacheView inside a streaming subtree bypass caching.
Stable API in .NET 11 RC2; GA reconciliation pending. Local memory execution does not prove distributed eviction or multi-node consistency.
constraints: Static SSR only; cache hits skip child lifecycle; isolate user-specific markup.
VaryByUser separates identities, not every permission claim. Include permission and content revisions in VaryBy; never use a shared anonymous key for private data.
Invalidation here changes a server-owned revision; old entries expire rather than being physically removed. Coordinate revisions across nodes before choosing a distributed provider.
HybridCache rejects ExpiresSliding. Use ExpiresAfter or ExpiresOn; CacheViewSizeLimit controls only the default memory store.
Cached child parameters are replayed unchanged. Do not rely on lifecycle authorization or fresh parent parameters on a hit. Reusable live-child contracts are separate guidance.

evidence.scope: Actual older Web SDK compilation. Separate real cookie-authenticated HTTP execution proves public data reuse and fresh per-user rendering.

Actual newer Web SDK compilation. Separate real SSR checks prove complete cache hits, skipped lifecycle, identity/query/permission variation, revision invalidation, expiry, concurrent misses, bypass and a negative leak fixture with both memory providers.

humanProof.scope: Bounded real static SSR HTTP checks run locally with actual cache providers and cookie identities. No required Human-only proof; distributed, multi-node, interactive and GA execution excluded.
